questions.solution:
Let, the lengths of the semi-major axis and semi-minor axis of the& ellipse are& $a$ & $b$ respectively, then the distance of the focus $\left(3,4\right)$ from the corresponding directrix $\left(x + y - 1 = 0\right)$ is equal to $\dfrac{a}{e} - ae$
$⇒ \dfrac{a}{\dfrac{1}{2}} - a\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \left|\dfrac{3 + 4 - 1}{\sqrt{2}}\right| = 3\sqrt{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{3a}{2} = 3\sqrt{2} ⇒ a = 2\sqrt{2}$
Distance between the focus and centre $= ae = \sqrt{2}$
The slope of the axis of the ellipse is $1 = tan ⁡ \theta$
$⇒ \left( cos ⁡ $\theta,$ sin ⁡ $\theta\right) = $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ or $\left(- \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$
The points on the axis of the ellipse at a distance \sqrt{2} units from $\left(3,4\right)$ are $\left(3 $\pm $\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right),4 \pm \sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right)
$⇒$Points are \left(2,3\right)$ or $\left(4,5\right)$ , but the centre is $\left(4,5\right)$ because it is far from the directrix as compared to $\left(2,3\right)$.

Given equation is$\dfrac{a2}{4} + b^{2} = 1$

Putting $a = 2cos ⁡ \theta, b = sin ⁡ \theta$, we get,

$2a + 3b= 2\left(2cos ⁡ \theta\right) + 3\left(sin ⁡ \theta\right) = 4cos\theta + 3sin\theta$
$⇒$ Minimum value $= - \sqrt{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = - 5$

questions.q: Two lines ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ of slope $1$ are tangent to $y^{2} = 4x$ and $x^{2} + 2y^{2} = 4$ respectively, such that the distance $d$ units between ${L}_{1}$ and ${L}_{2}$ is minimum, then the value of $d$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$y = x + 1$ is a tangent to $y^{2} = 4x$
$y = x \pm \sqrt{4 + 2}$ is a tangent to $\dfrac{x^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{2} = 1$
$⇒$ Minimum distance will be between the parallel lines
$y = x + \sqrt{6}$ and $y = x + 1$
$⇒ d = \dfrac{\sqrt{6} - 1}{2} = \sqrt{3} - \dfrac{1}{2}$& units

questions.q: A trapezium is formed by the pair of tangents of parabola $P: y = \dfrac{x^{2}}{4} + 1$ drawn from the centre of the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x^{2}}{4} + y^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$, tangent at the vertex of $P$ and the tangent at end point of the minor axis of $E$. The area (in sq. units) of the trapezium is
questions.solution:
The equation of the tangents from the centre of the ellipse to the parabola are $y = \pm x$

The equation of the tangent at the vertex $P$ of the parabola& is $y = 1$

The equation of the tangent at the end point of the minor axis of the ellipse is $y = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Hence, the area of trapezium $ABCD= \dfrac{1}{2} ⋅ \dfrac{1}{2} \left(1 + 2\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}$& sq. units

questions.q: The tangent to the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25} + \dfrac{y^{2}}{16} = 1$ at point $P$ lying in the first quadrant meets $x$-axis at $Q$ and $y$-axis at $R$. If the length $QR$ is minimum, then the equation of this tangent is
questions.solution:
Let point $P$ be $\left(5cos ⁡ \theta, 4sin ⁡ \theta\right), \theta \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$
So, the equation of tangent is $\dfrac{xcos ⁡ \theta}{5} + \dfrac{ysin ⁡ \theta}{4} = 1$
Points $Q$ and $R$ are $\left(5sec ⁡ \theta, 0\right)$ and $\left(0, 4cosec ⁡ \theta\right)$ respectively.
Hence,~${\left(QR\right)}^{2} = 25{sec}^{2} ⁡ \theta + 16{cosec}^{2} ⁡ \theta = 25 \left(1 + {tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta\right) +16 \left($1 + {cot}^{2} ⁡ $\theta\right)
$= 41 + 25{tan}^{2} ⁡ $\theta +$16{cot}^{2} ⁡ $\theta =$41 + ${ \left(5tan ⁡ \theta -4cot ⁡ \theta\right)}^{2} + 40$
${\left(QR\right)}_{min}^{2} = 81$ when ${tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{4}{5}⇒ tan ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$
Therefore,~$sin ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{2}{3},cos ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$
Hence, equation of tangent is $2x + \sqrt{5}y = 6\sqrt{5}$

questions.solution:
Since the minor axis is variable, hence& $e$ is a variable quantity

Therefore the equation of the tangent to the ellipse can be written as $\dfrac{xae}{a^{2}} + \dfrac{yb^{2}}{ab^{2}} = 1$
$⇒ ex + y = a ⇒ y - a + ex = 0$
This line passes through the fixed point~$\left(0, a\right)$ (where $a = 1$)

Hence, distance fro the centre of the ellipse~$= 1$

Equation of the normal at& $\left(3cos\theta, sin\theta\right)$ is $\dfrac{3x}{cos ⁡ \theta} - \dfrac{y}{sin ⁡ \theta} = 8$
So,~$ON = \left|\dfrac{- 8}{9{sec}^{2} ⁡ \theta + {cosec}^{2} ⁡ \theta}\right| = 2$~(given)
$⇒ 16 = 9\left(1 + {tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta\right) + \left(1 + {cot}^{2} ⁡ \theta\right) ⇒ 6 = 6 + \left(3tan ⁡ \theta - cot ⁡ \theta\right)2$

Hence,~${tan}^{2} ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{1}{3} ⇒ \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$
